purpose: Prove the canonical native replay authority is durable rather than process-local: two independently spawned runtimes that share only the durable store (never memory) must converge on one canonical identity with zero duplicate side effects.

runtime_independence.runtime_a: separate OS process (re-exec of the p12_7_cross_process_replay test binary)
runtime_independence.pools: each runtime constructs its own O3kStore connection pool, Placement ledger handle, ComputeService, NetworkService and provider

defects_exposed_and_corrected.symptom: an equivalent same-key create from the second runtime returned HTTP 409 because a name-conflict check saw the row the first runtime had just persisted under the same deterministic server identity
defects_exposed_and_corrected.correction: the pre-persistence name checks ignore the request's own deterministic server_id, so only a *different* live server with the same name conflicts; the canonical reservation resolves the equivalent write as a replay

defects_exposed_and_corrected.symptom: an equivalent replay response triggered the read-triggered create-convergence drive, dispatching a second provider create while the first runtime was still completing
defects_exposed_and_corrected.correction: canonical replay paths return the durable projection without the convergence drive; convergence stays owned by the accepting create, the poll surface, or the periodic sweep

defects_exposed_and_corrected.symptom: when a peer committed the deterministic allocation first, the losing scheduler attempt mapped PlacementError::InvalidAllocation to ComputeError::Conflict (HTTP 409) instead of converging
defects_exposed_and_corrected.correction: the scheduler re-observes the durable allocation on intent/commit/abandon placement errors and returns the existing decision, extending the rc.18 NoValidHost convergence to those paths

provider_dedup_boundary: The in-memory FakeComputeProvider keeps its idempotency ledger per process; the product dedups provider commands at the shared execution boundary (the compute-agent command journal, single-owner dispatch, covered by crates/o3k-compute/tests/multi_controller_acceptance.rs). The cross-process gate therefore asserts one deterministic provider identity across runtimes, and one dispatch in total.
